key_insight: Spray process selection strongly controls WC-10Co-4Cr coating density, hardness, wear, and corrosion performance, with HVAF and HVOF delivering the best overall tribological results and HVAF giving the best corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-critical steel components, switching from APS to denser high-velocity spray routes can markedly extend service life and reduce friction losses.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr coatings were deposited on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction/wear, and electrochemical corrosion behavior were compared.
Wear tracks were examined to identify dominant wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Compared with 304 stainless steel, the coatings reached hardness up to 1166.2 HV, reduced wear rate from 36.82×10^-5 to as low as 1.10×10^-5 mm3/N·m, and HVAF achieved the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr -0.37 VSCE, icorr 1.75 μA/cm², R 20438.5 Ω).
watch_item: Performance depends on spray-induced microstructure, so process tuning is critical and results may not transfer directly to different substrates, geometries, or service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
